evals.prompt: I wrote this article about AI transforming work for our company's thought leadership blog. Can you edit it to HBR quality? The file is at editing-hbr-articles-workspace/test-article-1-jargon-heavy.md
evals.expected_output: Edited article with jargon removed, throat-clearing cut, hedge words eliminated, vague evidence flagged or strengthened, active voice throughout, plus editorial summary

assertions.text: First paragraph does not open with throat-clearing phrases
No banned jargon terms remain (leverage, utilize, synergies, best-in-class, etc.)
No hedge words (perhaps, it seems, might as hedging)
Vague evidence replaced with specifics or flagged for author
Structured editorial summary with word count before/after
No more than 2 passive voice instances

evals.prompt: Here's my draft article on agentic AI in the enterprise. I want it publication-ready for a business audience. Please edit it. The file is at editing-hbr-articles-workspace/test-article-2-weak-evidence.md
evals.expected_output: Edited article with superlatives cut, promotional tone neutralized, vague claims flagged for specific data, balance added, plus editorial summary

assertions.text: No superlatives remain (revolutionary, game-changing, unprecedented, etc.)
At least 3 claims backed by named companies/figures or flagged
Structured editorial summary with changes and rationale

evals.prompt: This is a feature article I drafted about modern analytics platforms. It's way too long and I know it's repetitive. Can you tighten it up to HBR standards? File is at editing-hbr-articles-workspace/test-article-3-bloated-redundant.md
evals.expected_output: Significantly shortened article with redundancy eliminated, passive voice fixed, conclusion rewritten, word count reduced 25%+, plus editorial summary

assertions.text: Word count reduced at least 25% from original
Democratization concept stated once, not restated 3-4 times
No more than 5 passive voice instances
Conclusion doesn't repeat intro or re-summarize
Editorial summary includes before/after word count with percentage
